summary:
Step 6 is ACCEPTABLE. I reproduced the suite myself (`archive/tests/` → 392 passed, 16 failed, every failure pre-existing and unrelated: 13 skills-packaging, 2 `test_config_resolution` which fail with "async def functions are not natively supported" i.e. a missing pytest-asyncio plugin — not the environment leakage SCOPE.md's gloss suggests — and `test_fireworks_qwen`; `test_semantic_change_gate.py` alone → 37 passed). The shipped code agrees with §5.6, D5, D16, §12 #4, §15.8, §5.4 step 2 and §10; there is no unsound path (verified myself that `n_units = length work + length proofs` at semantic_store.ML:2308 makes the `n_units = 0` skip vacuous: `work = []` and `proofs = []` means `interpret_cone` is skipped at :2331 and the proofs fold does nothing, so no live `interpret_file` can ever run unchecked); and there is no hack. All eleven derivations are ruled: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 are right as they stand; derivation 4's conclusion is right but its justification sentence is not (see ml-ML-1); derivation 5's shape is right but its rendering of a `KeyError` is wrong (agreement-F3).

Three fixes are owed, none of them a defect in what the step does, and one proposal belongs to the user.

Fixes: (a) agreement-F3 — I reproduced the exact user-visible line and it carries a spurious pair of double quotes around the whole settings hint, because `str()` of a `KeyError` is `repr(args[0])` and `embedding_config.dimension` packs a human sentence into a `KeyError`; fix it at the source, in embedding_config.py, so every consumer is right. (b) py-F2 — I reproduced the test-hermeticity gap (`EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH=<a yaml without the default model> pytest -k startup` → 1 failed, 2 passed), and verified the corrected fix works (pin the template plus drop the loader cache through monkeypatch: without the pin 1 warning and the flag set, with it 0 warnings and the flag clear). (c) py-F1 — an elegance fix: below `interpret_with_parallel`, `cfg_context` has exactly two consumers and both are the identical expression `Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Context_Callbacks.static_context_unpacker cfg_context)` (:1834-1835 and :2279-2280), while three signatures carry two adjacent `Context.generic` parameters of opposite meaning that a swap would silently reverse — and the ML test cannot notice, because it passes the same value for both (Interpretation_Driver_Config_Test.thy:63-64). Building that callback once at the entry point and threading the `callback'` makes the D5 wiring type-enforced, deletes the duplicate construction, and makes §5.6's phrase "the same `Config.lookup` callback" literally true. Because it changes an exported ML signature and the ML test, and I am not permitted to touch an Isabelle process, that one is fix-then-rereview.

Rejected: ml-ML-1 (the remedy would turn a loud version skew into a silent run of the pre-gate pipeline) and py-F3 (no plan/code disagreement; the precedent it cites says the opposite of what it claims). agreement-F4 is a duplicate of py-F1 with a fix that does not work.

rulings.title: An RPC-level failure of the advisory startup check aborts a run that would otherwise have succeeded
rulings.rationale: The mechanism is real and I verified every link of it: Isabelle_RPC_Host/rpc.py:322-325 answers an unregistered procedure with write_error("Unknown procedure ...") and continues the loop; Tools/RPC.ML:376-388 and :547-549 turn that tag-1 reply into Remote_Calling_Failure; semantic_store.ML:2282-2283 hands it to interpretation_rpc_error, which is `error` in both branches (:1450-1453). I also confirmed the skew is constructible: `git show --stat` on 8683e6f, 5a3c201 and 0d279d7 shows steps 1-5 touched no Tools/*.ML at all, so the pre-step-6 ML half is wire-identical to what an older Python wheel pairs with. What the finding gets wrong is the value judgement. Steps 1-5 -- the entire semantic change gate -- live in the Python half. A Python half old enough to lack Semantic_Store.check_embedding_service is old enough to lack the gate, so swallowing the failure and carrying on does not 'degrade gracefully': it silently runs the pre-gate pipeline, writing records under the old rules while the user believes the gate is on. That is precisely what D10's failure principle forbids ('nothing ever mints a version silently or hides a failure'), and it is the opposite of this project's own precedent for a version skew: semantic_interpretation.py:1893-1901 RAISES on a mismatched wire entry with 'the Isabelle/ML and Python halves are from different releases. Install matching versions'. Aborting with 'Semantic interpretation RPC failed: Unknown procedure Semantic_Store.check_embedding_service' names the missing procedure and is diagnosable. Separately, the code comment on disk is accurate as written: :2271-2273 says 'A configuration problem never fails the run; only an RPC-level failure surfaces, as interpret_file's would' -- a statement about which failure class surfaces and how it is handled, both true. The false sentence ('it would have failed the first interpret_file anyway') appears only in SCOPE.md's derivation-4 prose, which is a review artifact, not a deliverable. Derivation 4's conclusion is accepted; its justification is corrected here.
rulings.fix: No code change. Derivation 4 is accepted with a corrected justification for the review record: an RPC-level failure of the check is fatal not because interpret_file would have failed anyway (an old Python half serves interpret_file fine), but because the only way this RPC can fail while the connection is healthy is a Python half that predates the gate, and running that half silently is worse than stopping. Do not adopt the proposed `handle Remote_Calling_Failure _ => ()`, and do not try to emit the mismatched-halves wording from ML -- that string lives in the Python half, which in this very scenario is the old one, and ML cannot honestly attribute an arbitrary Remote_Calling_Failure to a version skew.

rulings.title: The D5 wiring (Config.lookup served from cfg_context) is unpinned and one identifier away from silently breaking
rulings.rationale: I verified the hazard and, more importantly, verified that the shape fixing it is a net deletion. `grep -n cfg_context Tools/semantic_store.ML` shows that below interpret_with_parallel the parameter has exactly two consumers, and both are the same expression: `Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Context_Callbacks.static_context_unpacker cfg_context)` at :1834-1835 and at :2279-2280. Everything else (:1861, :1887, :2035, :2332, :2337) is pure threading. Meanwhile three signatures -- interpret_file_callbacks (:1825), send_for_interpretation (:1856-1857), interpret' (:1882) -- put two `Context.generic` parameters with opposite meanings side by side, so a swap type-checks and silently serves the prefilter's `Semantic_Embedding.embedding_model` from the cone node's rebuilt context, which is the exact D5 violation this step exists to prevent. The ML test cannot catch it: Interpretation_Driver_Config_Test.thy:63-64 passes `(Context.Proof \<^context>)` for BOTH parameters. And the trap is not imaginary -- the feared expression `Config.make_config_lookup_callback su` already exists, correctly, at :2473 inside query_knn, where `su` (:2463) is the single user-supplied context; a maintainer copying that line into interpret_file_callbacks, where `su` is the NODE's unpacker (:1828), gets the bug with no signal. (Note the finding's claim that no offline assertion could observe the captured context is false -- `callback'` and `connection` are both transparent (RPC.ML:3-5, :29) and the repo already drives BinIO over a temp file in Isabelle_RPC/test/Test_Term_Codec.thy -- but that does not change the fix.) I checked the fix is safe to share across the cone's parallel RPCs: mk_callback creates its `consumed` ref per action invocation, not per callback' value (RPC.ML:458-465), the function body is `Config.get` on an immutable context under registry_lock (config.ML:44-52), and call_command' builds `local_tab` fresh per call (RPC.ML:566-567). Elegance counts equally here: this replaces an invariant people must remember with one the type checker enforces, removes a duplicated construction, and shortens the five-line signature comment. It is fix-then-rereview rather than fix because it changes an exported ML signature and the ML test theory, and I may not touch an Isabelle process to compile it.
rulings.fix: Thread the built callback, not the context it is made from. In Tools/semantic_store.ML: (1) after the driver read at :2298 add `val config_cb = Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Context_Callbacks.static_context_unpacker cfg_context)` with a two-line comment saying it is built here, once, from the context the driver came from (D5). (2) Change the parameter `(cfg_context : Context.generic)` to `(config_cb : Remote_Procedure_Calling.callback')` in interpret_file_callbacks (:1825), send_for_interpretation (:1856), interpret' (:1882), interpret_cone (:2027) and check_embedding_service (:2274); pass `config_cb` at :1861, :1887, :2035, :2327, :2332, :2337. (3) Delete the local construction at :1834-1835 (cons the parameter onto the list instead) and the duplicate at :2279-2280 (`callback = [config_cb]`). (4) Signature at :31-37 becomes `val interpret_file_callbacks : Remote_Procedure_Calling.callback' -> Context.generic -> Remote_Procedure_Calling.callback' list`, with the comment shortened to what the type no longer needs to say. (5) Test/Interpretation_Driver_Config_Test.thy:62-70: build the callback in the test (`val cb = Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Context_Callbacks.static_context_unpacker (Context.Proof \<^context>))`) and pass it; keep BOTH assertions -- membership still guards the cons, and the exactly-one assertion still guards a second Config.lookup creeping in among the entity callbacks. Re-run the theory through the implementer's REPL server and re-review. §5.6 needs the hand edit listed in plan_edits.

rulings.title: Test 2 and 3 of the startup check depend on the machine's embedding_config; EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH, the documented test hook, is not cleared
rulings.rationale: I reproduced it: `EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH=<a two-line yaml with only text-embedding-3-large> python -m pytest archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py -q -k startup` gives `1 failed, 2 passed`, the failure being test_the_startup_check_accepts_a_configured_service_and_leaves_no_store_behind with `KeyError: "No 'dimension' entry for model 'Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B' ..."`. The fixture's own docstring (test_semantic_change_gate.py:729-732) promises 'the embedding environment cleared so only Config.lookup answers count', but it clears four variables and leaves the one the loader documents as the test hook (embedding_config.py:17: 'Set EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH to override the config file location (used by tests)'). Tests 2 and 3 construct a real provider, whose base __init__ does `self.dimension = cfg.dimension(model)` (semantic_embedding.py:288), so they read whatever YAML the machine resolves. I agree with the challenger that the finding overstates the trigger (the Qwen entry has been in the template since its first commit, so an old seeded user config cannot lack it) and that its proposed teardown is wrong (a fixture requesting monkeypatch is finalized BEFORE monkeypatch undoes the env var, so a teardown force_reload would re-read and cache the pinned template). But the gap is real, it is in a fixture that claims the property, and the fix is three lines. It also removes a second, quieter problem: with an Isabelle environment in the shell the tests otherwise read -- and if absent, create -- the developer's real $ISABELLE_HOME_USER/etc/embedding_config (User_Config.load copies the template into a missing path, _user_config.py:84-91); pinning EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH at the template makes path() resolve to a file that exists, so nothing is written.
rulings.fix:
In the `check` fixture, beside the four delenv calls at archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py:733-735, add:

    import Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding.embedding_config as EC
    monkeypatch.setenv("EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH", str(EC._CONFIG.template_path()))
    monkeypatch.setattr(EC._CONFIG, "_data", None)     # honour the pin; restored on teardown
    monkeypatch.setattr(EC._CONFIG, "_source", None)

Use the existing accessor `EC._CONFIG.template_path()` (_user_config.py:67-69) rather than rebuilding the path from `SE.__file__`. Clear the cache through monkeypatch, not through `load_embedding_config(force_reload=True)`: monkeypatch restores the previous cache when the fixture tears down, so no later test inherits the template's data, and no `yield` is needed. I verified this end to end with a probe that drove `_check_embedding_service` under a hostile EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH: without the pin, 1 warning and prefilter_disabled True; with the pin, 0 warnings and the flag clear. Optionally extend the docstring's 'the embedding environment cleared' to name the config file, since it is now genuinely pinned.

rulings.title: Step 6's three derivations are in no document: §5.6 still says the check runs unconditionally
rulings.rationale: There is no plan/code disagreement to record. §5.6 line 481 says the check runs 'once per cone run, in interpret_with_parallel before any theory starts'. I verified that with n_units = 0 no theory starts at all: n_units = length work + length proofs (semantic_store.ML:2308), so n_units = 0 forces work = [] and proofs = [], and then interpret_cone is skipped by `if null work` (:2331-2332) and the fold over proofs is vacuous (:2335-2339). A check that would govern nothing is not run; nothing the plan promises is lost. The precedent the finding invokes also says the opposite of what it claims: review_step5/SCOPE.md:127-161 carries the very same 'Derivations the implementer made' section with eleven entries and no accompanying plan edit, and the §15.5/§5.4 paragraphs were hand-edited later, as review fix #2 (review_step5/SCOPE.md:194-197). Accepted derivations that forced no code change were never absorbed into the plan -- the plan still writes `on_context_reset=noop` at :449 where the code has `lambda: None`. Both facts the finding calls undocumented are documented where this project puts load-bearing facts, in the source: semantic_store.ML:2325-2326 for the skip, :31-35 and :1819-1824 for the exported list. And §10's line (plan:726) is a description of what the ML test asserts, not an identifier needing a function to point at. The only real action is commit hygiene the precedent places after this review: bump the plan's Status line (plan:3-13) to name step 6 and its review record, as steps 4 and 5 did.
rulings.fix: No plan edit is owed by this finding. (§5.6 does need a hand edit, but for py-F1's fix, not for this -- see plan_edits.) At commit time, hand-edit the Status line at plan:3-13 to name step 6, its review record under ai-artifacts/review_step6/, and the fixes this review forced, in the same shape as the step-4 and step-5 entries.

rulings.title: §12 #4 tells the user "The system cannot continue." at the start of a run that then continues
rulings.rationale: Confirmed, and correctly classified. The text is reused verbatim: _missing_api_key_message() builds the paragraph whose second sentence is 'The system cannot continue.' (semantics.py:2741-2743); the single raise site is `raise RuntimeError(msg)` (semantics.py:2798, :2804); and §12 #4's approved slot is `str(exc)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1966-1967), so the whole retrieval paragraph rides in. I verified the run really does continue after that sentence on the `by aoa` path, which has no embed phase at all: toplevel.py:225-227 calls update_interpretations(connection, ask_user=True) inside a try/except; for a below-threshold workload semantics.py:1864-1874 runs the live cone through the Semantic_Store.interpret_theories callback, i.e. interpret_with_parallel, and the command then completes with no error -- which is exactly what D2 (plan:70) and §10 (plan:719-721) require, and what test_an_unconfigured_service_completes_the_run_with_every_gate_judged asserts. On the run_semantic_interpretation path the sentence becomes true only at the very end, after the whole LLM run has been paid for, when embed_phase() (Tools/interpret_command.ML:110-116) fails with the same message. Nothing here re-opens D16, which governs only the startup check's own double-print. Because §12 is 'User-visible texts -- all approved', the wording is the user's to decide, so this is a proposal, not a defect, and the implementer is plan-compliant as things stand.
rulings.fix: Put the choice to the user; change no user-visible wording without their explicit approval. Preferred shape, because it is a deletion and needs no new copy: drop the single sentence 'The system cannot continue.' from semantics.py:2743, leaving 'Semantic retrieval needs an embedding model to work, but no embedding service is configured.' On every pre-existing consumer the fatality is already carried by the channel -- the message is raised (semantics.py:2804) and rendered as an Isabelle error that stops the command (Tools/interpret_command.ML:113-116) -- so the sentence is redundant there and false at the new site; test_semantic_change_gate.py:757 asserts `_missing_api_key_message() in warnings[0]` and keeps passing untouched. If the user wants the sentence kept for retrieval, parameterize the FIRST paragraph (`_missing_api_key_message(situation=...)`, threaded through _resolve_embedding_config beside `warn`, which the same one caller flips) rather than appending a correction after the provider-doc URL ~14 lines below the sentence it corrects. Do not adopt the finding's option (a) as written: §12 #4's slot is str(exc) from one shared raise site, so making that exception carry the hint alone would strip the situation sentence from query_knn, embed_entities, contains and is_thy_embedded too.

rulings.title: §12 #4 renders a KeyError with stray double quotes around the whole message
rulings.rationale: I reproduced the exact user-visible line, twice: once by driving embedding_config.dimension directly, and once for real by running the startup tests under a config lacking the default model, where the recorded warning is `[Semantic_Embedding] The embedding service is not configured: "No 'dimension' entry for model 'Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B' in embedding config (...). Add it under 'dimension:'."` -- quotes wrapped around the whole hint. The cause is that `str()` of a KeyError is `repr(args[0])`, and because the message itself contains single quotes Python's repr picks double quotes. The unknown-model path is ordinary user reality (any model without a `dimension:` entry) and the implementer wrote test_the_startup_check_covers_the_provider_s_construction for it on purpose; that test asserts only `startswith(_NOT_CONFIGURED)` and `'no-such/model' in warnings[0]`, so the wart passes straight through. §12 #4's approved slot is '<existing message with the settings hint>', not the repr of that message, so correcting this brings the code closer to the approved text rather than changing it -- a fix, not a proposal. I prefer fixing it at the source over the challenger's rendering-site helper: the defect is that embedding_config packs a human sentence into a KeyError, whose __str__ is designed to repr a key. For an ordinary bare-key KeyError, repr IS the right rendering ('endpoint' names the key), so a site helper that unwraps every string-arg KeyError is wrong in the general case and has to be remembered at every future slot; a subclass fixes the one exception that is anomalous, everywhere, including the host log.
rulings.fix:
In Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/embedding_config.py, give the dimension error a KeyError subclass whose str() is its message, and raise it at :51-53:

    class Missing_Dimension(KeyError):
        """KeyError.__str__ is repr(arg); this arg is a settings hint the user reads."""
        def __str__(self) -> str:
            return self.args[0]

snapshot_sync.py:293-296 catches KeyError from dimension() and keeps working unchanged, and nothing else in the package depends on the repr. Then tighten the test so the wart cannot come back: in test_the_startup_check_covers_the_provider_s_construction (archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate.py:777-779) add

    assert conn.warnings[0].endswith("Add it under 'dimension:'."), \
        "the KeyError's message, not its repr"

I checked this assertion is False against the code on disk today (the line ends with a stray double quote after the period) and True once the subclass is in place, so it is a genuine mutation check rather than a restatement.

rulings.title: `driver` and `cfg_context` are threaded as two parameters although one determines the other, and the two adjacent Context.generic parameters can be swapped silently
rulings.rationale: Half A is refuted and half B is a duplicate. Half A says threading `driver` beside `cfg_context` is a redundant second thread; but the proposed `type run_config = {driver: string, cfg_context: Context.generic}` still stores both fields, so it removes a parameter, not the redundancy -- and the redundancy is deliberate and pre-dates step 6 (semantic_store.ML:27-29, :1849-1855 and the whole rationale of Interpretation_Driver_Config_Test.thy:1-13: the driver is resolved once at the entry and carried down as data so the cone cannot re-read it from a node). The record also hands interpret_file_callbacks a field it never uses and has to be unwrapped on the spot for check_embedding_service, which the fix itself concedes. Half B -- two adjacent same-typed context parameters that a swap would silently reverse -- is real, and I confirmed it independently, but it is the same defect as py-F1 and is fixed there by threading the built callback', which makes all three swappable pairs type-distinct without giving any function a parameter it does not use. One correction to the write-up for the record: its location list wrongly includes :2027; interpret_cone's `force : bool` sits between the two contexts, so nothing there is swappable, and interpret_with_parallel (:2295) takes only one context.
rulings.fix: No separate action. The surviving half is covered by py-F1's fix (build the Config.lookup callback once in interpret_with_parallel and thread the `Remote_Procedure_Calling.callback'`); do not introduce a run_config record, and leave `driver` as the once-resolved data it is.

The list gains `Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Universal_Key.static_context_unpacker cfg_context)` with `cfg_context` threaded from `interpret_with_parallel` through `interpret_cone` and `interpret'` beside `driver` (one ML parameter, no wire change; `interpret_with_parallel` calls `interpret'` directly for its `Context.Proof` roots at semantic_store.ML:2292 as well as through `interpret_cone` at :2287 -- both call sites): the user's context governs the prefilter (D5)."  PROPOSED: "`_resolve_embedding_config` issues `Config.lookup` callbacks (static context) and `send_for_interpretation`'s callback list has none.  `interpret_with_parallel` builds `Config.make_config_lookup_callback (Universal_Key.static_context_unpacker cfg_context)` once, beside the driver read, and threads that `callback'` -- not the context it was made from -- through `interpret_cone` and `interpret'` beside `driver` (one ML parameter, no wire change; `interpret_with_parallel` calls `interpret'` directly for its `Context.Proof` roots as well as through `interpret_cone` -- both call sites), where it joins the interpret_file callback list: the user's context governs the prefilter (D5), and because the threaded value is a callback rather than a context, no cone node's context can be substituted for it."  Hand-edit only (project rule: no scripted edits to plan documents).

§5.6, second paragraph (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:482-483) — same fix, so that "the same callback" is literally one value rather than a second copy of one expression. CURRENT: "one RPC `Semantic_Store.check_embedding_service`, carrying the same `Config.lookup` callback over `cfg_context`, resolves the embedding configuration".  PROPOSED: "one RPC `Semantic_Store.check_embedding_service`, carrying that same callback value, resolves the embedding configuration".

Status line (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:3-13) — at commit time, not now: it still reads "§13 steps 1–5 implemented ... steps 6–8 pending approval to start". Hand-edit it to name step 6, its review record `ai-artifacts/review_step6/` with `judge.json`, and the fixes this review forced, in the same shape as the existing step-4 and step-5 entries.
for_the_user: WORDING DECISION (py-F4) — the one user-visible line step 6 adds can tell you the system is about to stop, immediately before a run that keeps going. §12 #4 is "[Semantic_Embedding] The embedding service is not configured: <existing message with the settings hint>", and the existing message's second sentence is "The system cannot continue." (semantics.py:2742-2743). That sentence was written for semantic retrieval, where an unconfigured service really is fatal. Under D2 an interpretation run is not fatal: the prefilter is skipped and the judge decides alone. I checked the `by aoa` path specifically — it calls update_interpretations, which runs the cone and has no embedding phase afterwards — and the run there completes normally after the sentence has been printed. On the `isabelle_semantic_interpretation` command the sentence does become true, but only at the very end, when the separate vector-embedding phase fails, after the whole LLM run has been paid for. Three things you could decide: (1) delete just that sentence from the shared message — my recommendation, because it is a deletion rather than new copy, every other caller RAISES the message and Isabelle's error channel already carries the fatality, and the existing test that asserts the hint text keeps passing; (2) keep the sentence and give the message a per-caller opening sentence, so retrieval keeps today's text and the startup check gets a run-appropriate one; (3) leave it exactly as it is. Do not append a correcting sentence at the end: the message finishes with a provider documentation URL, so the correction would land about fourteen lines below the sentence it corrects. One further fact that belongs in this decision, which is outside D16's scope (D16 only governs the startup check's own double-print): on the `isabelle_semantic_interpretation` path the identical full hint is printed a second time later by the embedding phase's own resolution, so whichever wording you pick should read sensibly in both places.
